name: IntainMARKETS
shortDescription: IntainMARKETS is a digital asset-backed finance platform that brings issuers and investors, onto a common infrastructure for whole loan sales, credit facilities, and securitizations. It helps newer and smaller issuers access the full capital markets ecosystem with greater speed, transparency, and efficiency.
fullDescription:
IntainMARKETS is Intain’s asset-backed finance platform for digitizing issuance, administration, and settlement workflows across market participants on a shared, permissioned infrastructure. It combines AI-enabled due diligence, standardized data operations, and automated reporting/compliance processes, with optional tokenized issuance and digital settlement capabilities, to improve traceability, reduce manual reconciliation, and enhance operational efficiency.

IntainMARKETS is designed to facilitate a broader and more efficient asset-backed finance market by connecting newer and smaller issuers with investors, lenders, arrangers, verification agents, trustees and other ecosystem participants through a common digital infrastructure. By reducing transaction friction, lowering minimum viable deal sizes, and providing a shared, verifiable view of asset-level data, the platform supports more efficient execution of whole loan sales, credit facilities and securitizations, helping issuers access capital sooner while enabling investors to evaluate and participate in opportunities with greater speed, transparency and confidence.

name: Collateral Mobility Manager
shortDescription: Advanced solution for treasury and collateral desks, enabling margin management using tokenized assets across multiple blockchains.
fullDescription:
Advanced solution for treasury and collateral desks enabling entities to post or receive margin across various applications. Integrates margin calculation engines and supports tokenized assets as collateral from multiple blockchains.

The solution was deployed as the official sandbox in the GDF Tokenized MMF Collateral Working Group, which involved over 50 financial institutions and technology providers. This game changing solution provides superior efficiency and intraday liquidity management for treasurers and collateral managers.

Key orchestration plans include collateral movements, substitutions, intraday margin calls, liquidation and default scenarios.

These orchestrations were all demonstrated for UK and EU VM and IM - live in the GDF Industry Sandbox powered by Ownera. Link to demos and the full report below.

The Sandbox will be launching in the US in Q1 2026. Register here to get involved in the initiative alongside dozens of leading institutions: https://globaldigitalfinance.typeform.com/to/woIHpTZ1

videoGallery.description: Demonstrated an automated margin call workflow with Tokenovate, integrating tokenized collateral into existing systems—a key step toward scalable, straight-through TMMF margin calls. Participants: State Street, Lloyds, Tokenovate, Archax, Fireblocks
videoGallery.title: Demo 2: Simple Movement with MtM through Margin System (A) - Demonstrated an automated margin call workflow using third-party collateral management systems (Tokenovate) to calculate IM and VM requirements and trigger token transfers. This demonstration showed that tokenized collateral can be seamlessly integrated into existing collateral management infrastructure, bridging the gap between digital asset networks and traditional margining flows. It is a critical step toward full straight-through processing and scalability in using TMMFs for day-to-day margin calls.

videoGallery.title: Demo 2: Simple Movement with MtM through ZeroBeta calculation (B) - Demonstrated an automated margin call workflow using third-party collateral management systems (Zero Beta) to calculate IM and VM requirements and trigger token transfers. This demonstration showed that tokenized collateral can be seamlessly integrated into existing collateral management infrastructure, bridging the gap between digital asset networks and traditional margining flows. It is a critical step toward full straight-through processing and scalability in using TMMFs for day-to-day margin calls.

videoGallery.description: Demonstrated an MMF token de-peg using Kaiko price feeds, triggering automated on-chain substitution via DvD atomic swap—showcasing resilient, responsive tokenized collateral workflows. Participants: Schroders, Deutsche Bank, Tokeny Kaiko, ZeroBeta, Fireblocks.
videoGallery.title: Demo 3: Simple Movement with De-Peg of the Fund and DvD - Enacted a stress event wherein one posted MMF token “de-pegs” or drops in value (e.g. due to a market disruption in the underlying fund). In the test, a price feed from Kaiko was used to introduce a mock NAV drop for the token, causing its value to breach the haircut threshold. This triggered an automated substitution - the impaired fund is replaced with another eligible tokenized MMF via a Delivery-versus-Delivery (DvD) atomic swap orchestrated by Ownera routers between wallets. This scenario demonstrated the resilience and responsiveness of a tokenized collateral workflow to market events. In a traditional setup, such a fund value drop might require urgent calls and manual collateral substitution or cash funding; here it was handled automatically on-chain.

videoGallery.description: Demonstrated counterparty default, with the collateral taker unilaterally redeeming posted TMMF tokens into fiat—proving tokenized funds can be seized and liquidated on insolvency. Participants: ICCP (Ownera managed), ZeroBeta, Archax, Fireblocks.
videoGallery.title: Demo 4: Default of ICCP with Settlement in GBP (A) - Orchestrated a counterparty default during which the collateral provider fails to meet a margin call, allowing the collateral taker to enforce its rights on posted collateral. The pledgor (Party A) is assumed to default on variation margin payment. The secured party (Party B) then unilaterally redeems the posted TMMF tokens to cover the exposure. Variant methods tested: redemption into fiat (through normal fund processes). This was the most critical test from a legal enforceability standpoint. It demonstrated that a tokenized fund can be effectively seized and liquidated by a collateral taker even if the counterparty is insolvent or uncooperative. The successful unilateral redemption of the MMF tokens by the receiver proved the concept of “access on insolvency,” one of the key legal hurdles identified by the WG’s framework.

videoGallery.description: Demonstrated counterparty default, with the collateral taker redeeming TMMF tokens into tokenized cash via UBS—proving seizure and liquidation of tokenized funds on insolvency. Participants: ICCP (Ownera managed), Lloyds, ZeroBeta, Adhara, Fireblocks.
videoGallery.title: Demo 4: Default of ICCP with Redemption of fund using UBS Tokens (B) - Orchestrated a counterparty default during which the collateral provider fails to meet a margin call, allowing the collateral taker to enforce its rights on posted collateral. The pledgor (Party A) is assumed to default on variation margin payment. The secured party (Party B) then unilaterally redeems the posted TMMF tokens to cover the exposure. Variant methods tested: redemption into tokenized cash using a settlement token from UBS. This was the most critical test from a legal enforceability standpoint. It demonstrated that a tokenized fund can be effectively seized and liquidated by a collateral taker even if the counterparty is insolvent or uncooperative. The successful unilateral redemption of the MMF tokens by the receiver proved the concept of “access on insolvency,” one of the key legal hurdles identified by the WG’s framework.

videoGallery.title: Demo 6: Funding of TMMF in Triparty - This Sandbox really highlights the power of blockchain-based collateral mobility and how these innovative flows can be embedded within existing trading and collateral systems. name: LayerZero Cross-chain Asset Platform
shortDescription: A comprehensive platform for asset issuers to deploy, manage, and operate native multi-chain assets using LayerZero, with full administrative control, compliance tooling, and programmatic cross-chain distribution across 160+ blockchains.
fullDescription:
The LayerZero Multi-Chain Asset Platform provides institutional and crypto-native issuers with a complete toolkit to issue and manage assets natively across multiple blockchains—without token wrapping, liquidity fragmentation, or bespoke bridge integrations.

Issuers deploy assets using LayerZero’s OFT (Omnichain Fungible Token) standard and related primitives, enabling a single canonical supply that can move securely across EVM and non-EVM chains. The platform supports a wide range of issuer profiles, including stablecoin issuers, tokenization platforms, financial institutions, transfer agents, CSDs, and crypto protocols.

The application combines on-chain primitives with centralized institutional tooling, enabling issuers to enforce compliance rules, manage permissions, and orchestrate cross-chain asset flows at scale. It integrates natively with the LayerZero messaging layer and aligns with Ownera / FinP2P distribution and settlement workflows.

Core capabilities include:
	•	Native multi-chain issuance across EVM and non-EVM chains using OFTs
	•	Unified total supply management with cross-chain mint/burn semantics
	•	MABA and Lockbox workflows for controlled issuance and custody models
	•	Centralized admin tooling for allow-listing, permissions, and smart-contract configuration updates
	•	Cross-chain asset management APIs for programmatic transfers and treasury operations
	•	Compliance controls including investor access rules and whitelisting
	•	Value Transfer API to move issuer-owned or permissioned assets across chains
	•	Data API providing real-time visibility into cross-chain movements, balances, and network activity
	•	Decentralized Verifier Network setup for institutions seeking to own their end-to-end security

Business outcomes:
Issuers gain faster time-to-market for multi-chain assets, reduced operational complexity, and a single control plane for global distribution. By standardizing cross-chain issuance and lifecycle management, the platform enables assets to interoperate seamlessly with downstream applications—such as trading, settlement, collateral, and payments—without custom integrations.
orchestration: Issuer-native orchestration of multi-chain deployments, minting/burning, supply synchronization, cross-chain compliance gating, investor onboarding, and distribution flows.

name: Confidential Collateral Pool
shortDescription: Private Collateral Pool enables multiple banks or large financial institutions to lend money to each other quickly and securely, using valuable assets as a safety net (collateral), without anyone outside of the specific transaction knowing exactly what assets are being moved around or how much money is being handled. This ensures privacy in a highly competitive market where confidentiality is critical.
fullDescription:
The App operates as follows:

1. Setup and Preparation

The FIs agree to use this new confidential system. The confidentiality infrastructure use Secure Multi Party Computation (MPC) to safeguard and protect the data owned by counter parties. This infrastructure allows onchain contracts performing calculations on encrypted data (balances, collateral amounts, etc.).

2. Posting the Collateral

Bank A wants to borrow money from Bank B. Bank A must first lock up sufficient collateral in the smart contract pool.

Bank A encrypts the amount of tokens it is depositing (as a collateral) and sends a transaction to the confidential collateral management smart contract.

Privacy Feature: Thanks to Soda Labs' MPC infra, the confidential collateral management smart contract can receive and operate on encrypted values. Observers (blockchain scanners) only see random-looking data moving on the public ledger. The total size of the collateral pool as well as the share of each counter party remains secret.

3. Monitoring the Collateral Position

Both banks need to continuously verify that there is enough safety net in place as the market value of the collateral changes.

The confidential collateral management smart contract constantly runs calculations on the encrypted data to make sure the value of the collateral relative to the amount borrowed without ever revealing either number publicly.

4. The "Margin Call" Trigger (Risk Management)

If the value of the collateral drops suddenly (e.g., the stock market crashes, and the stocks used as collateral are worth less), the borrower must add more assets to the pool to maintain the safety net.

The smart contract has a built-in function that uses an off-chain price feed (an oracle) to check current market prices. This calculation happens confidentially. If the calculation determines the collateral value is too low, it automatically flags the account for a margin call—an automated alert requiring the borrower to top up their collateral.

5. Withdrawing or Settling the Collateral

Once the loan is fully repaid (settled), Bank A is entitled to get its original collateral back.

Bank A initiates a withdrawal request. The smart contract verifies that the loan obligation is settled and releases the confidential tokens back to Bank A's wallet.


Terms:

[Tokenized Collateral] means converting a real-world asset (RWA)—like a US Treasury bond or a share of stock—into a digital, blockchain-based token. Each token represents ownership of that underlying asset. In this architecture, these tokens are confidential, meaning only the owner knows how many they have, even though the token lives on a public blockchain.

[Collateral Position]: This is simply the status of the assets held as security—is there enough coverage, or is there a shortfall? The collateral management contract can automatically verify the health of this position privately.

[Settling Collateral]: This term refers to the final act of returning the assets to the original owner after all obligations (the loan repayment) have been satisfied.
orchestration: Collateral poisition and risk across lenders, borrowers and price feeds

name: LayerZero Cross-chain Connector
shortDescription: A developer-focused utility that enables applications to send messages, transfer value, and synchronize data across chains using LayerZero’s secure cross-chain infrastructure.
fullDescription:
The LayerZero Cross-Chain Connector is a lightweight SuperApp designed for builders who want to extend their applications beyond a single blockchain—or integrate directly with LayerZero-enabled assets and protocols.

Using LayerZero’s OApp (Omnichain Application) framework, developers can send arbitrary messages, initiate cross-chain value transfers, and consume cross-chain data without managing bridges, relayers, or chain-specific infrastructure. The Connector abstracts cross-chain complexity into simple, composable APIs that integrate cleanly into existing smart-contract and backend architectures.

This application serves three primary use cases:
	1.	Applications transmitting arbitrary data across multiple chains (e.g., sending corporate action data)
	2.	Applications utilizing or moving LayerZero-native assets (e.g., USD stablecoins that are OFTs)
	3.	Applications importing or reacting to cross-chain data and events (e.g., custom monitoring)

Core capabilities include:
	•	Generic OApp messaging for arbitrary cross-chain contract calls and state sync
	•	Value Transfer API for programmatic cross-chain movement of tokens and assets
	•	Data API for querying cross-chain activity, execution status, and analytics
	•	Chain-agnostic design supporting EVM and non-EVM environments
	•	Composable architecture that integrates with DeFi, payments, RWAs, gaming, and enterprise apps

Business outcomes:
Developers can ship multi-chain applications faster, reduce infrastructure overhead, and expand their addressable market without rewriting core logic per chain. For businesses, the Connector enables cross-chain product expansion, shared liquidity, and unified user experiences—powered by a single, battle-tested interoperability layer.
orchestration: Cross-chain smart contract invocation, asset movement, and messaging across 154+ blockchains via LayerZero’s ultra-light node protocol. Supports multi-chain settlement, token actions, and interoperability for all SuperApps.

metrics.type: Network Coverage (157+ blockchains), Transaction Throughput, Cross-Chain Message Volume.

name: Munivestor’s Digital Bond Marketplace
shortDescription: Munivestor is a financial technology company on a mission to democratize and expand the $4 trillion municipal securities market. We enable cities to raise capital directly from investors globally. Our regulated online marketplace empowers cities to create, market, and sell securities directly to investors of all sizes. Investors can also make secondary market purchases through Munivestor along with tracking market data. We are building a democratized global municipal finance marketplace that empowers communities to interact directly with the world.
fullDescription:
Many U.S. cities, especially smaller municipalities, face real challenges when it comes to accessing affordable capital for critical infrastructure and sustainable development projects. The reality is, while the municipal bond market is a $4 trillion arena, with roughly $400 billion in annual issuance, it’s not keeping up with the projected need—an estimated $750 billion annually by 2050—to achieve environmental sustainability goals.

The way things stand, traditional underwriting models provided by large investment banks have their strengths. They bring deep expertise, a guarantee of bond sale even in rough market conditions, and access to a vast network of institutional investors. But here’s the thing; that model works best for large deals above $50 million, which aligns with their scale and cost structures. The average municipal issuer does not fit this mold and get hit with steeper costs when accessing the market.

There’s also a broader issue: these investment banks are set up to serve their biggest clients, which can limit how broadly they market a bond issuance. This isn’t a criticism; it’s just how their business works. It leaves a gap, though—a gap Munivestor is ready to fill.

Munivestor steps in to offer an alternative issuance model that’s built for a different kind of market reality—one where cities have more control over their bond offerings, where the costs are more predictable and manageable, and where transparency is not an afterthought but a fundamental part of the process. Our digital marketplace opens up the field to both retail and institutional investors, providing an expanded pool of potential buyers and a more inclusive approach to financing. And with our focus on sustainable and impact-driven projects, we’re aligning with the growing demand for investments that don’t just deliver returns but also make a difference.

Munivestor is built to serve several key players in the municipal finance ecosystem, but we’re starting with a clear focus: Municipalities looking to issue bonds for general purposes, housing, economic development, and environmental projects. These sectors are ripe for innovation, and our network already spans these areas, connecting us with the issuers who are ready to try something new. Here’s a breakdown of who we’re targeting:

Municipalities/Bond Issuers: We’re talking about the 50,000+ potential municipal bond issuers across the U.S. These are the cities, counties, states, school districts, universities, transportation agencies, utility authorities, development agencies, and green banks that need to finance public projects like schools, clean energy, affordable housing, roads, bridges, hospitals, and more.

Bond Investors: This is the demand side of the equation—the buyers. Our online issuance model greatly expands an issuer’s investor base by including small investors across the planet. While foundations, pension funds, and corporations haven’t historically been major players here (because tax-exempt income doesn’t benefit them), they’re starting to pay attention due to the growing alignment with ESG and impact goals.

Market Professionals: Municipalities don’t go it alone—they rely heavily on professionals like bond attorneys, municipal advisors, and special project managers to execute bond transactions. Our platform is designed to integrate these professionals seamlessly into the process, giving them access to a municipality’s administrative panel to help manage online bond sales more efficiently
orchestration: Munivestor facilitates a primary and secondary online marketplace for tokenized municipal bonds. Issuers and investors are allowed to connect directly.

name: Prove Know Your Payee
shortDescription: Prove’s Know Your Payee is an identity verification solution that confirms the identity of a payment recipient before funds are sent, helping organizations prevent fraud, reduce misdirected payments, and improve trust.
fullDescription:
Prove’s Know Your Payee is a real-time identity verification solution designed to confirm that a payment recipient is legitimate before funds are sent. By validating the identity behind account details such as a phone number or payment credential, it helps financial institutions, fintechs, and enterprises reduce fraud, prevent misdirected payments, and increase confidence in digital transactions. This is particularly valuable in an environment where scams like authorized push payment (APP) fraud and social engineering are on the rise, and where traditional account validation methods alone are no longer sufficient.

The solution leverages Prove’s phone-centric identity network, which combines telecom, device, and behavioral signals to establish a high-confidence link between an individual and their payment credentials. By analyzing these signals in real time, Know Your Payee can determine whether the recipient matches the expected identity, flag anomalies, and provide actionable risk insights before a transaction is completed. This approach enables organizations to move beyond static account verification toward dynamic, identity-based decisioning that works across multiple payment rails, including ACH, cards, and real-time payments.

In addition to fraud prevention, Know Your Payee enhances the user experience by introducing greater transparency and trust into the payment process. End users can have more confidence that they are sending money to the correct person or business, while organizations benefit from reduced losses, fewer disputes, and stronger compliance with evolving regulatory expectations. The result is a more secure and seamless payment ecosystem, where identity assurance is embedded directly into the transaction flow rather than treated as a separate step.

With mobile-centric verification and real-time validation of business and applicant data, organizations can onboard legitimate businesses faster while minimizing fraud risk.

Result: faster onboarding, higher completion rates, and stronger trust from the start.
fullDescription:
Prove Pre-Fill® for Business enables fast, frictionless onboarding by instantly connecting an individual applicant to a verified business, using just a few inputs. By leveraging Prove’s phone-centric identity and the Prove Identity Network®, it pre-populates and verifies business and applicant data in real time, eliminating manual form entry and accelerating decisioning.

Designed for modern B2B onboarding, Pre-Fill for Business reduces abandonment, improves conversion rates, and helps organizations onboard more businesses—faster—without compromising security. Its mobile-centric authentication and dynamic verification checks ensure that applicants are legitimately associated with the business, preventing impersonation and fraud.

With real-time verification of business data (including EIN/TIN and documents), customizable workflows, and cross-channel support, organizations can make smarter risk decisions while delivering a seamless user experience.

The result: higher onboarding completion, lower fraud risk, and a streamlined path to revenue.

name: ProveX
shortDescription: ProveX℠ is a digital trust exchange that enables instant access to verified data and credentials, unlocking seamless, secure experiences across the customer journey.
fullDescription:
ProveX℠ is a digital trust exchange that transforms verified identity into instant access to trusted data and credentials from a growing ecosystem of partners. Once a user’s identity is confirmed, businesses can securely retrieve and apply verified information—such as payment credentials, credit signals, and compliance data—in real time.

By enabling trust to persist across channels and interactions, ProveX eliminates the need to repeatedly verify users at every step. This allows organizations to orchestrate seamless, personalized experiences, from onboarding to checkout, while maintaining strong security and privacy controls.

Built on a tokenized identity framework with cryptographic binding and consent-driven data exchange, ProveX ensures that every request is securely tied to an authenticated individual. The result is a unified foundation for accessing verified data, reducing friction, improving efficiency, and enabling smarter, trust-driven customer experiences at scale.
